newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Air HK follows surcharge with rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Air HK follows surcharge with rates rise.

text.p: Air Hong Kong (AHK) is increasing its rates ex-Europe from November 11, the carrier's European general manager, Marcel Buelens told Reuters.
The increases are likely to be around the two to three percent level, he said in a telehone interview.
The Hong Kong all-cargo carrier already introduced rates increases in September. The airline pushed its rates up by 10 percent on certain destinations, such as Europe to Dubai, Japan and Hong Kong.
The carrier, 75 percent owned by Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, introduced a US 10 cents a kg surcharge from November 5, he added.
"We were one of the first carriers to introduce rates increases out of Europe. But we had to introduce them to give the airline an acceptable future and keep the aircraft flying."
"In the last six months the carriers have had to subsidise the fuel increases. Prices of fuel have increased by 20 to 30 percent," he said.

"Many colleagues are selling below their costs. It is a highly competitive industry but we have to add these increases to survive," Buelens added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
